country: Multiple (DRIAMS Switzerland, MS-UMG Germany, MARISMa Spain)
sample_unit: experiments (over 15,000 across 13 methods, 5 transfer scenarios, 5 seeds)

links.outcome: Domain gap closed by fine-tuning with target-site labels versus unsupervised adaptation, cross-site AMR prediction
links.effect: Fine-tuning with target-site labels closes 92%-97% of the domain gap; unsupervised DA methods yield only 0%-6% improvement over source-only baselines.
links.quote: The results demonstrate that simple fine-tuning with target-site labels closes 92%-97% of the domain gap and dominates all unsupervised DA methods, which yield only 0%-6% improvement over source-only baselines.

links.outcome: Cross-site performance degradation of models trained at one hospital site
links.effect: Models trained at one hospital site suffer substantial performance degradation at another site due to differences in instruments, sample preparation, and patient populations.
links.quote: However, models trained at one hospital site suffer substantial performance degradation at another site due to differences in instruments, sample preparation, and patient populations.

unlisted_practices: Collecting a modest number of labeled target-site samples (as few as 25%) to recover 81%-94% of full supervised performance

screen.practice: local recalibration/fine-tuning with target-site labels before deployment
screen.reason: Evaluates domain adaptation and local fine-tuning deployment practices to address cross-site performance degradation in clinical AMR prediction.

primary.practice: local validation and fine-tuning with site-specific labels
